description: The figure presents three pie charts comparing the distribution of four categories (N+K+, N−K+, N−K−, N+K−) across three difficulty levels labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard,” with a total of four slices in each pie and percentage values printed inside the slices. In the “easy” chart, the teal N+K+ slice is about 55.4%, the yellow N−K+ slice about 38.3%, the orange N−K− slice about 4.6%, and the red N+K− slice about 1.7%. In the “medium” chart, the teal N+K+ slice is about 58.8%, the yellow N−K+ slice about 35.4%, the orange N−K− slice about 4.0%, and the red N+K− slice about 1.8%. In the “hard” chart, the orange N−K− slice is about 37.9%, the yellow N−K+ slice about 37.3%, the teal N+K+ slice about 18.1%, and the red N+K− slice about 6.7%. A legend on the right maps colors to labels (teal=N+K+, yellow=N−K+, orange=N−K−, red=N+K−), no slices appear exploded or offset, and the ordering of slices around each pie is consistent rather than strictly arranged by descending size.
